evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Joanna: 'I just need about ten to fifteen minutes if this is a good time.' — framing present but rep doesn't explicitly state 'you can walk away with a quote you can depend on' or wait for explicit yes before moving into concerns.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Joanna: 'do you have any important concerns or instructions about this move that you also want to discuss on this call?' — asked very early, but after Rachel has already started unprompted disclosure. Structured as 'important concerns' rather than the rubric's 'what are your biggest concerns about this move, and what do you want answers to.'
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Rachel raises multiple concerns: garage/shed packing, safe (£300), treadmill, horse trailer loading, truck capacity from last move. Joanna follows up on nearly all: 'I don't think it's this email...maybe I can check that out' (prior move context), 'do you have like, pretty much the same amount of stuff or you just have a little bit more in the garage and then the shed', 'is it for the whole house or just the garage', 'Do you have any extra rooms', 'Is it just on the ground or is it...no stairs involved', 'Aside from those two items, large items that you've mentioned anything else', 'how about large Radle items, paintings, artworks', and a full follow-up on the horse trailer waiver requirement and manager approval.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Joanna acknowledges concerns throughout ('Mm-hmm', 'Okay, no problem') but never summarizes or reflects back: 'So what I'm hearing is...' type language is absent.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Joanna: 'Typically for a house this size once everything's all packed and wrapped up in terms of the items that you put two boxes, we might end up with about 142 A 180 boxes in total.' — range given. Also mentions '...usually we end up using about $558 worth of packing supplies.' Then: 'Now typically for a house the size, usually we conduct like a virtual walkthrough, it's like a video call of the house just to assess how much items we're packing and moving for you in order for us to give you a more personalized estimate.'
evidence_quotes.walkthrough_offered: Joanna: 'Now typically for a house the size, usually we conduct like a virtual walkthrough, it's like a video call of the house just to assess how much items we're packing and moving for you in order for us to give you a more personalized estimate and I understand that may still change depending on how much you know, you plan to pack yourself or is there items or letting or whatnot. So but yeah, just in case are you available to do that...' Rachel: 'Yeah, we can do that at some point when we're more certain I think.' — Walkthrough correctly offered and accepted; move routed cleanly to virtual walkthrough before final pricing locked.

top_strength: Joanna gathered comprehensive logistics details (three bedrooms, garage, shed, safe weight, treadmill, wheelchairs, grill, mirrors, parking at both locations, one-story homes, prior-move history) and followed up persistently on customer concerns, going multiple layers deep on the horse trailer loading and truck capacity issues.
coaching_note: Add an explicit active-listening summary ('So what I'm hearing is garage packing, the horse trailer loading question, and your truck capacity from last time — did I get all of it?') before routing to the walkthrough, and ensure the quid-pro-quo framing in Section 1 includes the full promise of 'a quote you can depend on' and a clear wait for yes before pivoting to concerns.
